choices: Makes the method faster by bypassing virtual dispatch
Tells the compiler you intend to override a parent method — errors if the method doesn't actually override anything
Prevents subclasses from overriding the method
Creates a new method that shadows the parent's method
explanation: @Override is a compile-time safety check. If you misspell the method name or have the wrong parameters, the compiler reports an error rather than silently creating a new overloaded method. Always use @Override when overriding.
